We've seen a number of posts on X from AI3 vehicle owners receiving V14 Lite via 2026.20.6.10, who were not in the initial wave.

At this time, this second wave appears to be very small (~<0.2% of eligible vehicles), and all vehicles have been notified via the Tesla mobile app.

🚨 Important PSA regarding 2026.20.200.1 (if originating from a build with Full Self-Driving V14.3 or later).


Teslascope (@teslascope)

This is a very rare occasion (and perhaps the first) where we are actively suggesting Tesla owners to NOT install this update.

Installing 2026.20.200.1 will also wipe and disable Full Self-Driving streaks.

If and when there is additional information, we will share it here.



— https://nitter.net/teslascope/status/2079365625059910014#m
Here to answer any and all questions that we can, otherwise, more information can be found in the quoted post above.

Specifically, we believe the rollout of 2026.20.200.1 was not intentional, given that drivers are being reverted from Full Self-Driving V14.3.4 back to V14.2.2.5.

From all appearances, this appears to be an erroneous rollout and that it WAS meant to be a factory build.


Joey (@JoeyV1117)

Same thing happened to me @teslascope what’s going on? I took delivery on June 5th.







— https://nitter.net/JoeyV1117/status/2079358351729729755#m

This is a very rare occasion (and perhaps the first) where we are actively suggesting Tesla owners to NOT install this update.

Installing 2026.20.200.1 will also wipe and disable Full Self-Driving streaks.

If and when there is additional information, we will share it here.

PSA: It appears @Tesla is no longer following their historically consistent .100 through .300 versions meaning factory updates.

Alongside the recent European software release 2026.21.100, this is now the second software update not to follow long-standing versioning conventions.


Teslascope (@teslascope)

As such, we will be updating our software update posts (such as the one quoted above) to mention that this may not necessarily be a factory update.

We, however, encourage @Tesla / @Tesla_AI to revert to the prior pattern so drivers can be better educated and to avoid confusion.

We're pleased to share that @Tesla has enabled Self-Driving telemetry metrics for AI3 vehicles starting on 2026.20.6.10!

This means that tracking and leaderboard participation on our app will be automatically enabled for all AI3 vehicles once you receive V14 Lite.

The new FSD v14 lite build adds the Self-Driving app INCLUDING streaks!!

For our Plus and Pro subscribers, AI3 vehicles will also automatically begin recording Self-Driving usage per drive upon receiving the update.

We’ll also be expanding our existing Self-Driving data visualizations on both web and iOS in the following week.

The feature "Start Self-Driving from Park" has a new addition to its notes in 2026.20.6.10:

Brake Confirm requires the driver to press and release the brake pedal before FSD (Supervised) can be activated. When Brake Confirm is disabled, pressing the button will allow Self-Driving to apply the brakes and engage FSD (Supervised).

If driver detection requirements are not met or if FSD (Supervised) does not detect a driver, you will be required to press and release the brake pedal to confirm. You can enable Brake Confirm in Self-Driving > Brake Confirm.
